html:
Michael III was emperor of the Byzantine Empire from 842 to 867, the last of the Amorian dynasty. He came to the throne aged two. His mother Theodora ruled for him, and in 843 she restored the veneration of icons, ending Iconoclasm.

From 856 he ruled with his uncle Bardas, an able minister who backed learning in Constantinople. In these years:

  • In 858 Michael deposed the patriarch Ignatius and raised the scholar Photios, a layman, which led to the Photian schism with Rome.
  • In 860 the Rus' attacked Constantinople by sea for the first time.
  • In 863 a Byzantine army crushed an Arab raiding army at Lalakaon, a turning point on the eastern frontier.
  • In 863 he sent Cyril and Methodius to Moravia, and soon after Khan Boris of Bulgaria was baptised with Michael as godfather, the conversion of Bulgaria.

His favourite, the groom Basil, murdered Bardas in 866, was crowned co-emperor, and in 867 had Michael killed in his bedchamber, founding the Macedonian dynasty. Writers under that dynasty called Michael "the Drunkard"; historians now treat that picture with caution.
